subject: astronomy
title: Solar System: Sizes & Distances
welcome_lead: Space is huge — let's get a feel for just how huge.
meta_desc: KS3 astronomy: scale of the solar system, AU, comparing sizes.
final_note: Models help, but real space is even more empty than you imagine.

concepts.def: How model size relates to real size.
Distance light travels in one minute.
Largest planet — about 1300 Earths could fit inside.

walkthroughs.body_html: One AU = the average Earth-Sun distance (about 150 million km). Mars is about 1.5 AU; Jupiter about 5 AU; Neptune about 30 AU.
The Sun's diameter is about 109 Earths. Jupiter is about 11 Earths wide. Mercury is about a third of Earth's width.
If Earth were a peppercorn, the Sun would be a beach ball 26 metres away. Most of space is just empty.
